Norwegian Agriculture Firm Fjellgrønt AS Files for Bankruptcy Amid Difficult Market Conditions

Norwegian agricultural producer Fjellgrønt AS has filed for bankruptcy, citing prolonged financial difficulties and challenging market conditions. The company, based in Hedmark, is one of the region's established growers of root vegetables and grains, with roughly 60 employees. The bankruptcy process, initiated in the district court this week, has led to an immediate suspension of all trading and production activities at Fjellgrønt’s main facility.

“The board has made every effort to secure the company’s future, but the combination of weak harvests and declining margins made it impossible to continue,” said CEO Lars Øverland in a statement. “This is a very difficult day for our dedicated staff and for the region’s agricultural community.”

According to court documents, Fjellgrønt AS reported accumulated losses exceeding NOK 24 million over the past two years. The company’s fields and storage sites are now being evaluated by the appointed administrator, who will assess the options for asset realization.

“The bankruptcy of Fjellgrønt AS underscores the volatility and financial pressures facing Norwegian agriculture,” said Ingunn Sørmo, senior analyst at the Norwegian Agriculture and Food Confederation. “Many producers have struggled with increased input costs and unpredictable weather patterns in recent seasons.”

In the coming weeks, the administrator will review claims from creditors and determine the fate of the company’s remaining stock and assets. Employees have been notified, and local union representatives are assisting them with next steps.

At the time of writing, Fjellgrønt’s operations remain halted and its future uncertain, pending further proceedings in the bankruptcy case. No timeline has been given for possible liquidation or sale of the business.
